traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and requirements for docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are implemented and verified. The `prefer-implements-annotation` rule exists, is registered with the plugin, and is disabled by default, making it an optional migration aid. It detects legacy `@story` + `@req` combinations, issues configurable recommendation diagnostics, and applies conservative ESLint auto-fixes that rewrite single-story, simple patterns into a single `@supports` line while preserving comment formatting and structure. Multi-story and mixed-annotation patterns are detected and reported without auto-fix, and complex story/req lines are explicitly left unfixed to avoid invalid output. Backward compatibility is maintained: comments using only `@story`, only `@req`, or only `@supports` remain valid and are not flagged by this rule, and the existing validation rules continue to operate unchanged. A user-facing migration guide documents the rule’s purpose, configuration (off/warn/error), and behavior, matching the story’s documentation requirement. Tests in `tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts` explicitly exercise REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION, and REQ-VALID-OUTPUT, and all pass in the recorded Jest run. Given this concrete evidence, the story is fully implemented.
